status_summary: No executive or legislative action returning civilian investigations to OPM was found for 2025-01-20 through 2026-10-11. A GAO statement to a House Oversight subcommittee on 2026-02-24 says DCSA conducts about 95 percent of government background investigations, around 2 million a year, and that DOD projects finishing NBIS modernization by the end of FY2027 and retiring legacy systems in FY2028; the legacy systems still reside on OPM's network under interagency agreements. DefenseScoop reported on 2026-02-25 that DCSA had an acting director and that an updated estimate projects about 2.2 billion dollars more for NBIS through FY2031.

timeline.event: GAO testifies to the House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations that DCSA conducts about 95 percent of government background investigations and that DOD projects finishing NBIS modernization by the end of FY2027.

title: Return civilian clearance and suitability investigations from DCSA to OPM
uncertainties: Absence of evidence: neither the GAO statement nor the DefenseScoop report mentions a plan to move investigations back to OPM, general web searches (including one in review) returned only 2019 and 2020 coverage of the original transfer, and a Federal Register query for presidential documents on background investigations since 2025-01-20 returned no results. Proposals in unpublished drafts, Congress or OPM planning would not appear. The NDAA text was not searched for investigation-transfer provisions.
